newsitem.title: UK: UK drinks body issues tough industry code.
newsitem.headline: UK drinks body issues tough industry code.

text.p: Britain's drinks industry body The Portman Group said on Thursday it has issued a tougher code of practice to retailers and brewers of alcohol in an effort to limit under-age drinking.
The industry code will be backed up by government measures, to be announced at 1000 GMT, aimed at making so-called "alcopops" -- alcoholic lemonade and soda drinks -- less attractive to youngsters.
Britain's Home Secretary Jack Straw asked for an urgent inquiry into the sale of alcopops in May.

But industry sources said they do not expect the ministerial group, headed by Home Office minister George Howarth, to ban the products after publication of the Portman Group's revamped code of conduct.
The code, drawn up by the self-regulatory drinks industry watchdog, funded by seven major manufacturers, will cover all drinks over 0.5 percent alcohol by volume.
It will tighten restrictions on the packaging and labelling of drinks to ensure they do not appeal especially to under 18 year olds.

That means banning references to illegal drugs, linking a drink with sexual prowess or success, using images of people under 25 or look as if they are under 25 and using artificially-bright colours or child-like lettering.
The colour, taste and texture of a drink will also be taken into account by the Independent Complaints Panel.
Retailers will be asked not to stock those products if a complaint is upheld, and local licensing authorities may take action against shop keepers who fail to respond.
Portman Group director Jean Coussins said in a statement: "manufacturers and retailers who ignore the code will pay a high price, socially and commercially."
"The vast majority of the drinks industry has already shown its strong commitment to the code.
"The new enforcement measures are designed to ensure that offending products are squeezed out of the market," she added.

Top selling "alcopops" are more than five percent alcohol by volume and the choice of flavours available is growing. In January the Advertising Standards Authority ruled that the market leader Hooper's Hooch, brewed by Bass Plc should drop a cartoon character of a smiley lemon from its logo and change the bottle's design after complaints.
The drinks have proved a runaway success for the industry. Sales now exceed 250 million pounds a year and it is now the fastest growing sector in the drinks industry.
Other alcopop brands include Two Dogs made by Merrydown Plc and Whitbread Plc's Vanilla Heist and Lemon Jag. Supermarkets also now have their own label brands like Sainsbury's Piranha.
